about:
Allied Steel Fabricators, Inc. was founded in 1984 by Michael Exe in Redmond, Washington. The company began in a 1,200-square-foot building focusing on structural steel projects. It remains family-owned and operated by the Exe family, with founder Mike Exe's legacy continuing after his passing in 2003.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication including sheet metal laser cutting (with a Trumpf TruLaser 3030 Fiber 6,000-watt system), shearing to 10 feet, sawing, press brake forming up to 12 feet and 325 tons, MIG/TIG and stud welding, finishing (time-saver sanders, prime coating, powder coating, plating), structural steel fabrication with a 6-ton overhead crane and iron workers, handrail fabrication and installation, and custom crating and shipping via two 20-foot trucks. Facility expansions in 1986 and 2003 doubled the footprint, adding a dedicated structural steel building and a larger retail division workspace.

Allied Steel serves architectural, structural steel, retail display, furniture, and custom fabrication markets. Early work on unique structural features attracted corporate display managers from major retailers, leading to custom display stands for local retailers alongside handrail services for area contractors. The company describes its range as "from earrings to I-beams," producing items from small decorative pieces to large structural assemblies for commercial and residential projects.

The company's stated differentiators are its family-owned consistency, American-made production in Washington, and a motto of "Old World Craftsmanship with Modern Day Style." Its mission emphasizes exceeding customer expectations while fostering employee growth, and its vision targets process and market expansion to insulate stakeholders from economic fluctuations.
